status: primary-document routing evidence; no hardware measurement or DSP change
finding: Post-filter overdrive is the natural published block-level reading: the official specification assigns overdrive to AMP, and audio diagrams place AMP after FILTER. No inspected diagram labels a separate OD node or explicitly specifies its internal position relative to amp-envelope multiplication.

evidence.fact: Grey audio arrows place MIX/MOD before FILTER before AMP before EFFECTS. OVERDRIVE is absent as a distinct node. Black arrows describe controls.
Each Upper/Lower tone has FILTER feeding AMP; AMP ENV controls AMP. EFFECTS explicitly contains DELAY then REVERB. No separate OVERDRIVE node is shown.

evidence.context: The latter is an indented specification entry under AMP, alongside its Level knob and envelope. This is stronger than merely seeing a button in the AMP panel.

evidence.fact: Overdrive switch and drive parameters belong to the AMP group; they specify on/off and distortion amount, not processing order.

evidence.type: text plus visually inspected page39 control/waveform illustration
evidence.fact: Overdrive control is pictured in the AMP panel. The text describes tube-like distortion, added harmonics and using the button plus LEVEL to change drive; its generic boost/clipping illustration contains no filter or envelope routing.
The AMP chapter explicitly says the oscillator signal processed through FILTER is amplified here. OVERDRIVE appears in the pictured AMP panel, but no separate distortion route is described.

classification.overdrive_after_filter: corroborated architectural inference from the two preceding facts; not a separately labelled OD routing statement
classification.overdrive_before_filter: not supported by the inspected sources

scope: Cached official English Owner’s Manual and Roland Synthesis101 were inspected. Relevant PDF diagrams/specification pages were rendered and visually checked.
